Title: HTTP rate limiting
Objective: Implement CDR-008 section 8 per-session and per-account API request ceilings at the api layer
Security considerations: Keyed on the server-verified session and account, never on IP: with no deployment configuration there is no trusted proxy, so a forged x-forwarded-for would both evade the limit and let an attacker spend a victim bucket. Keys stored as sha256 digests, never raw. Refusal body is the generic envelope - no limit value, no remaining balance, no scope name.
Tenant considerations: Table is global and un-RLSed by design (migration 0005 precedent): a session bucket is consulted before any tenant context exists. Rows carry no tenant data - a digest, a count and a timestamp.
Approval or policy considerations: None - a frequency ceiling is not an approval or policy decision
Audit behavior: None. Deliberate: one audit row per throttled request would let a flood drive unbounded audit growth, turning a protection into an amplifier (CDR-082 section 4). Observable via the structured log line.
Usage behavior: Writes NOTHING to usage_events. A usage event means metered work happened; a throttled request did none, and inflating the ledger would make the NFR-015 spend cap and the launch-gate-7 reconciliation disagree with reality (CDR-082 section 5).
Failure behavior: Fail-closed: an unreadable bucket refuses, reported as unavailable (503) rather than throttled (429), because we could not tell is a different claim from you are sending too many requests.
Acceptance criteria: Session and account ceilings enforced on every authenticated apps/web route at CDR-008 section 8 values; a route that stops reaching the ceiling fails the build; SQL bucket arithmetic proven to agree with the pure specification against real PostgreSQL; concurrent consumers cannot exceed the ceiling.
Required tests: Pure token-bucket spec suite; real-PostgreSQL differential suite replaying the spec cases plus concurrency, grants and CHECK constraints; enforcement tests through resolveVerifiedIdentity including the ordering assertion that a throttled request never reaches the Clerk Backend API; static coverage checker with its own negative probe.
Verification procedure: pnpm run check; node tools/check-rate-limit-coverage.mjs; hosted CI with zero skips for the real-PostgreSQL suite
Rollback or recovery: Migration 0055 down drops the table; it holds only transient counters, so a rollback costs at most one refill window of leniency.
Documentation changes: CDR-082; SECURITY-VERIFICATION-PLAN Authentication row note; REQUIREMENT-TRACEABILITY NFR-010 and ACC-001 rows; REQUIREMENT-TO-TICKET-TRACEABILITY NFR-010 row

Security considerations: Every value is chosen so it cannot break Clerk sign-in, and one was REMOVED for failing that test: COOP shipped as same-origin-allow-popups and was withdrawn under independent review, because the premise (Clerk opens an OAuth popup) is not establishable in this repository - clerk-js is not installed, no social provider is configured - and the fuller analysis says COOP on the callback page CAUSES the window.opener loss it was claimed to prevent; COOP is enforcing, so unlike the report-only CSP it cannot be published then corrected (CDR-083 s6.2).
